prompt: Create a Go HTTP handler file with a single GET /hello endpoint returning JSON {"message": "hello, world"}, 200 status, and error for non-GET. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'handlers/hello.go'.
spec: Create a Go HTTP handler with a single GET /hello endpoint that returns a JSON response {"message": "hello, world"}. Include proper Content-Type header, status code 200, and an error response for non-GET methods. Follow standard net/http patterns.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Code compiles, handler returns valid JSON with correct status codes

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All spec requirements implemented: GET handling, JSON response, method check

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Follows Go idioms: proper error handling, net/http patterns, package declaration

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: No unnecessary code, imports, or abstractions

prompt: Add a Validate() error method to the User struct checking ID, Email (@), Name, and Age (0-150). You MUST use the replace_file_content or write_file tool to update 'models/user.go'.
spec: Add a Validate() error method to the User struct that checks: ID is non-empty, Email contains '@', Name is non-empty, and Age is between 0 and 150. Return a descriptive error for the first failing check. Do not modify existing methods or fields.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Validate method compiles and returns correct errors for invalid inputs

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All four validation checks implemented as specified

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Follows Go error handling patterns, consistent with existing code style

criteria.name: Preservation

prompt: Create a TypeScript config parser with validation for port, host, logLevel, and database, including env loading. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'src/config.ts'.
spec:
Create a TypeScript module that:
1. Defines a Config interface with fields: port (number), host (string), logLevel ('debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error'), database (object with url: string, maxConnections: number)
2. Exports a parseConfig(raw: unknown): Config function that validates the input against the schema, throwing descriptive errors for missing/invalid fields
3. Exports a loadConfigFromEnv(): Config function that reads PORT, HOST, LOG_LEVEL, DATABASE_URL, DB_MAX_CONNECTIONS from environment variables with sensible defaults (port=3000, host='localhost', logLevel='info', maxConnections=10)
4. Use no external dependencies

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: TypeScript compiles, validation catches invalid inputs, types are sound

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: Both parseConfig and loadConfigFromEnv implemented with all fields and defaults

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic TypeScript: proper typing, no 'any', discriminated unions for logLevel

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Clean validation logic without over-engineering

prompt: Add exponential backoff retries (3x) and 10s timeouts to the WeatherClient class. You MUST use the replace_file_content or write_file tool to update 'weather/client.py'.
spec:
Update the WeatherClient class to add:
1. Retry logic: retry failed requests up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s delays)
2. Timeout: each individual request should timeout after 10 seconds
3. Custom exceptions: define WeatherAPIError(status_code, message) and WeatherTimeoutError for specific failure modes
4. All three methods (get_current, get_forecast, get_alerts) should use the retry/timeout logic
5. Keep the existing method signatures compatible — callers should not need to change

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Retry logic works with exponential backoff, timeouts applied per-request

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: Custom exceptions defined, all three methods wrapped, retry count and backoff match spec

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Pythonic patterns: context managers, exception hierarchy, type hints

criteria.name: Preservation
criteria.description: Existing method signatures and class interface unchanged

prompt: Create a thread-safe generic LRU Cache[K, V] with TTL and maxSize eviction. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'cache/lru.go'.
spec:
Create a Go package that implements a generic LRU cache:
1. Type Cache[K comparable, V any] with New(maxSize int, defaultTTL time.Duration) constructor
2. Methods: Get(key K) (V, bool), Set(key K, value V), SetWithTTL(key K, value V, ttl time.Duration), Delete(key K), Len() int, Clear()
3. LRU eviction: when maxSize is exceeded, evict the least recently used entry (Get counts as use)
4. TTL expiration: entries expire after their TTL; expired entries are removed on access (lazy eviction)
5. Thread safety: all methods must be safe for concurrent use via sync.RWMutex
6. Include package-level documentation explaining the eviction policy

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Generic types compile on Go 1.21+, LRU order maintained, TTL expiration works

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All methods implemented, lazy eviction on access, capacity-based eviction on Set

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic Go generics, proper mutex usage (RLock for reads), meaningful doc comments

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Clean doubly-linked list or container/list usage without over-abstraction

prompt: Refactor auth middleware to support pluggable BearerToken and APIKey strategies via an interface. You MUST use the replace_file_content or write_file tool to update 'middleware/auth.go'.
spec:
Refactor the auth middleware to support pluggable authentication strategies:
1. Define an AuthStrategy interface with method Authenticate(r *http.Request) (identity string, err error)
2. Implement BearerTokenStrategy (existing behavior) and APIKeyStrategy (reads X-API-Key header, validates against a key set)
3. The AuthMiddleware function should accept a variadic list of strategies and try each in order, succeeding on the first match
4. On successful auth, set the identity in the request context using a package-level context key
5. If all strategies fail, return 401 with a JSON error body {"error": "unauthorized", "strategies_tried": [...]}
6. Keep the package name as 'middleware'

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Interface properly defined, strategies implement it, fallthrough logic works

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: Both strategies implemented, context propagation, JSON error response with tried list

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Clean interface design, context.WithValue with typed key, proper Go patterns

criteria.name: Preservation
criteria.description: Bearer token validation logic preserved in BearerTokenStrategy

prompt: Create a type-safe TypeScript EventEmitter supporting wildcards (*) and chainable methods. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'src/events/emitter.ts'.
spec:
Create a TypeScript module implementing a type-safe event emitter:
1. Generic class EventEmitter<Events extends Record<string, unknown[]>> where keys are event names and values are argument tuples
2. Methods: on(event, handler), once(event, handler), off(event, handler?), emit(event, ...args), listenerCount(event)
3. Wildcard support: on('*', handler) subscribes to all events; the handler receives (eventName, ...args)
4. once() handlers automatically unsubscribe after first invocation
5. off() without handler removes all handlers for that event
6. Methods should be chainable (return 'this')
7. Export a createEmitter<Events>() factory function
8. No external dependencies

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Type inference works for event args, wildcard handlers receive correct types

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All methods implemented: on, once, off, emit, listenerCount, wildcards, chaining

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Advanced TypeScript: mapped types, conditional types where needed, no 'any' leaks

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Clean internal data structure without unnecessary complexity

prompt: Add cursor-based (base64) pagination with nextCursor/hasMore to the list handler. You MUST use the replace_file_content or write_file tool to update 'handlers/list.go'.
spec:
Update the list handler to support cursor-based pagination:
1. Accept query parameters: cursor (string, opaque), limit (int, default 20, max 100)
2. The cursor encodes the last seen item's ID (base64-encoded for opacity)
3. Response shape: {"items": [...], "nextCursor": "abc...", "hasMore": true}
4. When cursor is provided, return items after that cursor position; when empty, start from the beginning
5. Add a helper function EncodeCursor(id string) string and DecodeCursor(cursor string) (string, error)
6. Add input validation: limit must be 1-100, invalid cursors return 400
7. Keep the ItemStore and Item types unchanged

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Cursor encoding/decoding works, pagination returns correct slices, edge cases handled

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All query params parsed, validation implemented, response shape matches spec

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Clean Go HTTP patterns, proper error responses, base64 cursor encoding

criteria.name: Preservation
criteria.description: ItemStore and Item types unchanged, existing Add/All methods preserved

prompt: Create a fluent SQL QueryBuilder for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE with $1 placeholders and sanitization. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'db/query.go'.
spec:
Create a Go package implementing a fluent SQL query builder:
1. Type QueryBuilder with methods: Select(columns ...string), From(table string), Where(condition string, args ...any), Join(joinType string, table string, on string), OrderBy(column string, direction string), Limit(n int), Offset(n int), GroupBy(columns ...string), Having(condition string, args ...any)
2. All methods return *QueryBuilder for chaining
3. Build() (string, []any) returns the SQL string with $1,$2,... placeholders and collected args slice
4. Support INSERT: InsertInto(table string), Values(row map[string]any) → Build() returns INSERT INTO ... VALUES ($1, $2, ...) with deterministic column ordering
5. Support UPDATE: Update(table string), Set(column string, value any) → Build() returns UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE ...
6. Input sanitization: table and column names must match [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* pattern; reject others with error
7. Build() returns an error if required clauses are missing (e.g., SELECT without FROM)
8. Signature: Build() (string, []any, error)

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Generated SQL is valid, placeholders correctly numbered, args in correct order

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE all supported, joins, groupBy, having, ordering, limit/offset

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Fluent API design, clear internal state machine, proper Go error patterns

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: No unnecessary abstractions, clean string building, regex validation

prompt: Refactor notifications to use a Notifier interface with discriminated union payloads (Email/Sms/Push). You MUST use the replace_file_content or write_file tool to update 'src/notifications/notifier.ts'.
spec:
Refactor the notification module from class inheritance to interface-based composition:
1. Define a Notifier interface: { send(payload: NotificationPayload): Promise<NotificationResult> }
2. Define NotificationPayload as a discriminated union: EmailPayload | SmsPayload | PushPayload, each with a 'type' discriminant field
3. Define NotificationResult: { success: boolean; messageId?: string; error?: string }
4. Implement each notifier (EmailNotifier, SmsNotifier, PushNotifier) as standalone objects implementing Notifier, using a shared sendRequest helper (not inheritance)
5. Create a CompositeNotifier that accepts Notifier[] and dispatches to the correct one based on payload type
6. Export a createNotificationService(config: { apiUrl: string; apiKey: string }) factory that returns a CompositeNotifier with all three channels configured
7. All types and interfaces must be exported
8. Preserve the same API endpoint paths (/email, /sms, /push) from the original implementation

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Discriminated union narrows correctly, composite dispatch works, types are sound

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All interfaces defined, three notifiers implemented, factory function, composite dispatcher

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic TypeScript composition: no classes, discriminated unions, proper generics

criteria.name: Preservation
criteria.description: Same API endpoints used, same HTTP method and auth header pattern preserved
